newsitem.title: USA: BP quarterly dividend seen worth $1.05/ADR.
newsitem.headline: BP quarterly dividend seen worth $1.05/ADR.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc said the quarterly dividend announced Tuesday, on the basis of current tax law and practice, would be worth $1.050 per American Depositary Receipt to qualifying U.S. resident ADR holders.
The record date for ADR holders is November 19 with payment to be made on February 3, the company said.

The current double tax convention between the U.K. and the U.S. includes provisions which entitle qualifying U.S. resident ADR holders to a refund of the currently applicable U.K. tax credit attaching to the dividend, less a currently applicable 15 percent U.K. withholding tax charged on the sum of the dividend and the tax credit.

The company said the effect of these arrangements for qualifying U.S. resident ADR holders is that currently the tax credit would raise the value of the dividend announced by the board from $0.988 to $1.235 but the 15 percent withholding tax would reduce it to $1.050 per ADR. Subject to certain limitations, that withholding tax, currently worth about $0.185 per ADR, may be treated as a foreign income tax, eligible for credit against the ADR holder's federal income taxes.
BP said the rate of exchange of $1.6469 to the pound used to translate BP's dividend on ordinary shares into U.S. dollars was that in effect at 1700 GMT/1200 EST on November 4.
